name: Infamous Baali Through the Ages (Clanbook Lore)

text.content:
Many different Cainites have claimed the name "Shaitan" through the ages, spinning contradictory tales of his history, intentions, and powers; most of these impostors are long since fallen to dust. Only one survives to this day, and he truly believes himself to be the original Shaitan. This pretender would appear to be a product of Nergal's machinations several centuries past, though nothing more is known of his true origins. He first made his presence known in Toledo in al-Andalus, where he served as Magister of the infernal Black School, a college dedicated to the dark arts. Unlike Nergal, who cared more for spreading the worship of Namtaru, this Shaitan specialized in guiding others down the path of infernalism itself.

It took decades for other @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} to discover the impostor's whereabouts, and in the meantime he taught summoning rituals and true names of power to mortals and depraved Cainites alike in a frenzy of educational fervor. Before the Black College was finally smashed by his own bloodline, its graduates had already spread infernalist teachings far and wide across Europe and into northern Africa — a legacy of corruption that survives independent of the man who seeded it.

Cybele was a childe of Shaitan — though precisely which of the many Cainites to claim that name may never be known. Embraced in the maddening corridors of the Knossos Labyrinth, she learned her craft from its whispers and advanced along paths of corruption and power far quicker than any of Shaitan's other progeny. When Thera erupted, she was among the few acolytes who escaped Crete, carrying with her the knowledge that Moloch's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} had betrayed her sire.

Cybele became Moloch's chief adversary following the destruction of Crete, growing in power far quicker than any could have anticipated as she dedicated her unlife to fighting her sire's betrayer. When Carthage sent Hannibal forth in the Punic Wars, Cybele helped Rome defeat the African general, and her actions in the city's defense earned her praise and power from Rome's other Cainites, who remained unaware of her lineage. Her advancement undid itself, however: she suffered from a terrible blood-lust that sent her on murderous rampages through her own temples, and though her Cainite supporters in the Roman Senate tried to suppress the matter, the truth of her origins was eventually whispered in the Forum. Romans regarded her cult with fear thereafter, especially during festivals when her eunuch galli priests danced in the streets, cutting themselves and performing public rites of self-castration, and Cybele's growing isolation only fed further, bloodier rampages.

Cybele's ultimate fate remains a mystery following the fall of Carthage. It was her rituals that sealed Troile and Moloch in the earth, where they still sleep to this day, but she never accompanied the Roman armies back to Italy; the last reliable sighting placed her aboard a ship bound for Crete, seeming tired and spent, as though the years of hatred had taken their toll. Nearly a millennium later, unsubstantiated rumors place her at the pit of Iblis-al-Akbar during the ritual that cursed the Assamites, identifying herself as Decani and blessing the elixir of cursed blood; those who knew her say she served Namtaru, her sire's master. If Cybele found her way back into the Labyrinth after Carthage's destruction, she may have also found Namtaru — and taken one of his 36 names to become Decani.

Azaneal, leader of the new @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} movement, is the undisputed ruler of Chorazin and the first Cainite to galvanize the bloodline since Shaitan himself. Although he lacks his predecessor's charisma, Azaneal remains a potent adversary: physically an imposing figure with eyes of almost solid black and a near-palpable aura of darkness, and mentally lacking Shaitan's subtlety but compensating for it through sheer strength of will.

Despite the forces he gathers, Azaneal has no intention of repeating his predecessors' mistakes. He claims he seeks to unite the bloodline under his dominion and to usurp the Elders of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} — and enough of the bloodline are anxious enough for a unifying leader to follow him for exactly that reason. His true agenda, however, is to uncover all the secrets of Chorazin: he believes Shaitan meant the town not as an end unto itself, but as a gate through which eternal darkness would enter the world, though he does not know how to complete Shaitan's unfinished work.

One key Azaneal believes he lacks is the body of Namtaru, the Baali master of shadows. He has sent several Cainites to Crete to uncover the Labyrinth, but his agents have all vanished; he suspects the infamous Decani guard the Labyrinth and are destroying his servants, and feels he cannot yet fight them directly. Instead he concentrates on creating fertile childer and subjugating the Baali of Europe, hoping that with a united bloodline behind him he might one day take Crete and return Namtaru to Chorazin.

Once concubine of the king of a long-dead Akkadian city-state, this former protégé of the fiendish high priest Anaduk the Black has risen remarkably quickly through the ranks of her hellish bloodline. Her extraordinarily calm, unruffled nature is legendary even among the Childer of Caine: when she acts, she does so quickly and without confusion, and like many others of her kind she works alone, preferring solitude to the company of others. Those few Cainites who have met and spoken with her note that she goes covered and veiled in the tradition of Islam, though some whisper she is concealing some disfigurement. She bears an especial hatred for the children of Arikel, ensnaring, seducing, and torturing any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} unfortunate enough to cross her path or trespass on her holdings — a hatred whose origin none are sure of, though piles of ash throughout Europe testify to her efficiency.

Ma-ri-ah has ingratiated herself to several greater powers, including the horrid Decani and their peers; more terrifying still, she serves no less an entity than the Child called Anoster, Lord of Despair, a feat truly exceptional for one of her standing. With this potent backing she has turned her attentions to Byzantium, its tenuous relations with the Western Church, and the great games of power all too frequently played there.

Rumors regarding Ma-ri-ah's eccentric, solitary nature and twisted motives abound. Some name her traitor to her own kind and call her a murderess responsible for the destruction of her sire; others believe she is not @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} at all, but a subversive agent of other powers, perhaps Setite or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}. One fragmented Eblaite tablet claims she has evolved beyond the limitations of mortal and Cainite existence altogether, becoming a dark and hungry goddess made flesh. Whatever the truth, "Mary" has become a dangerous, wild-card figure waist-deep in the politics and intrigue of the Dark Medieval world — and as always, the nail that stands too tall is inevitably hammered down.

Many older @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} orders have abandoned the Levant for Europe or the uncharted East, marshaling their forces far from those who know and hunt them; the land between the Tigris and Euphrates will always be their home, but it is no longer safe for them. A greater concern looms, however. Through the bloodline's own laxity and weakness, too many true names have slipped out into the world, uncontrolled and unbidden, bringing the Sleepers closer to waking than they have been since the days of the first tribe. Mysterious plagues boil forth with increasing frequency, and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} know this to be evidence that Namtaru is stirring; those who know the legends of the Children fear that once Namtaru awakens, the other sleeping Antediluvians will not be far behind.

The bloodline is now divided over what to do about this. Some hide, or seek ways of undoing the impossible, hoping that by rediscovering the oldest true names — the first names of the Children — they might find a way to control the Antediluvians' actions once they rise, for should current trends continue, the Children will wake in wrath and hunger, beholden to none. Others instead seek to hasten the awakening, hoping that by doing reverence unto the Sleepers now, they might be spared in the coming dark days. And across Europe, careless and ignorant younger Baali cavort and name themselves "Mephisto," shouting names of power that echo between the worlds with no notion of what they might summon. All true Baali know that the end is coming, and if asked, most will say they believe it is coming very soon.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Baali, Appendix: To Reign in Hell / Appendix II: Of Interest to Scholars and Chirurgeons
